items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: when I got playing with the bands and got around is when I really realised that the lack of education and I wanted to learn. So I got to go on the road with Ben Pollack's band and orchestra which at that time consisted of Benny Goodman, Glen Miller was also in the band, the Pollack band.

ctx.x: I'd asked you to comment upon him and ...
Glen Miller as you know, people that you knew.

items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: Glen did the arranging and we had a great small band... So Jack came with the band, Glen did the arranging

ctx.x: And goodness gracious. But Benny was, now he was always for his family. He always saw that they were well taken care of. But he was quite frugal a good business man. An excellent business man. And Glen, Glen Miller, he was quite a guy. He was the task master. He used to arrange. And man I know that the Black Hearth there, he came in with an arrangement, we used to rehearse after the job. He came in there with an arrangement one night that we were going to record and there were some tough parts in there you know.
And I said, hey Glen, I said this is tough man this part. Can't you change it? He says, no. He says, take it home and woodshed it Jimmy. He said, it will make a better musician out of you.

items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: I know later on I used to play tennis with him down in New Orleans.

ctx.x: I was speaking about Glen what Miller and a very interesting guy he was. And I said he was a task master. And he was also a very competitive guy. I know later on I used to play tennis with him down in New Orleans. And he was an excellent tennis player. And believe me, I was nothing on tennis. You know mediocre, very mediocre. But Glen would like to smash that ball. This was the kind of, his character you know. He wanted to hit that ball hard and smash it over so you couldn't even get

close to it.
So he kept trying that on me and I said, want to play a dollar a game? And he said, certainly. (LAUGHTER). Well certainly you know, and I know he could have beat me. So us said, well give us some incentive. And we played a dollar a game and he didn't win one game. (LAUGHTER). He didn't win game number one. He would get madder and madder and he'd smash that ball so hard and it keep going into the net or it would go over the line. And I think I won, oh I don't know, ten or eleven dollars from him.…
